title: spreadr: A R package to simulate spreading activation in a network

(2011), viewed activation fixed cognitive resource “spread” among connected nodes network.

title: spreadr: A R package to simulate spreading activation in a network
text: Simply pass weighted network (igraph object adjacency matrix) spreadr function. Let’s take simple three-node network example:  let node "" initial activation = 10, expect see 9 units activation go "c", 1 unit "b", retention = 0.
code: weighted_network <- matrix(   c(0, 1, 9,     1, 0, 0,     9, 0, 0), nrow=3, byrow=TRUE) colnames(weighted_network) <- c("a", "b", "c") rownames(weighted_network) <- c("a", "b", "c")  # To visualise the network only --- this is not necessary for spreadr weighted_igraph <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(   weighted_network, mode="undirected", weighted=TRUE) plot(weighted_igraph, edge.width=E(weighted_igraph)$weight) spreadr(   weighted_igraph, data.frame(node="a", activation=10),   time=1, retention=0, include_t0=TRUE) ##   node activation time ## 1    a         10    0 ## 2    b          0    0 ## 3    c          0    0 ## 4    a          0    1 ## 5    b          1    1 ## 6    c          9    1

title: spreadr: A R package to simulate spreading activation in a network
text: Simply pass directed network (igraph object adjacency matrix) spreadr function. Let’s take simple three-node network example:  let node "b" initial activation = 10, expect see 10 units activation go "c", none go "", retention = 0.
code: directed_network <- matrix(   c(0, 1, 0,     0, 0, 1,     0, 0, 0), nrow=3, byrow=TRUE) colnames(directed_network) <- c("a", "b", "c") rownames(directed_network) <- c("a", "b", "c")  # To visualise the network only --- this is not necessary for spreadr directed_igraph <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(   directed_network, mode="directed") plot(directed_igraph, edge.width=E(directed_igraph)$weight) spreadr(   directed_igraph, data.frame(node="b", activation=10),   time=1, retention=0, include_t0=TRUE) ##   node activation time ## 1    a          0    0 ## 2    b         10    0 ## 3    c          0    0 ## 4    a          0    1 ## 5    b          0    1 ## 6    c         10    1

what: Repeating the simulation across different parameters
title: spreadr: A R package to simulate spreading activation in a network
text: ways , showcase relatively simple method using data.frames. Suppose want simulate spreading activation across four different parameter sets (retention, decay): (0, 0), (0.5, 0), (0, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5). first record parameters differ data.frame: , prepare common parameters differ. Now, run simulate set different parameters, simply apply rows params.
code: params <- data.frame(   retention=c(0, 0.5,   0, 0.5),   decay=    c(0,   0, 0.5, 0.5)) network <- matrix(   c(0, 1,     0, 0), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE) start_run <- data.frame(node=1, activation=10) apply(params, 1, function(row)   spreadr(     network, start_run,     time=2, include_t0=TRUE,     retention=row[1], decay=row[2])) ## [[1]] ##   node activation time ## 1    1         10    0 ## 2    2          0    0 ## 3    1          0    1 ## 4    2         10    1 ## 5    1          0    2 ## 6    2         10    2 ##  ## [[2]] ##   node activation time ## 1    1       10.0    0 ## 2    2        0.0    0 ## 3    1        5.0    1 ## 4    2        5.0    1 ## 5    1        2.5    2 ## 6    2        7.5    2 ##  ## [[3]] ##   node activation time ## 1    1       10.0    0 ## 2    2        0.0    0 ## 3    1        0.0    1 ## 4    2        5.0    1 ## 5    1        0.0    2 ## 6    2        2.5    2 ##  ## [[4]] ##   node activation time ## 1    1     10.000    0 ## 2    2      0.000    0 ## 3    1      2.500    1 ## 4    2      2.500    1 ## 5    1      0.625    2 ## 6    2      1.875    2
